headline: Compute money lands; K-12 is the strategy's blind spot
digest: Ottawa's new AI Sovereign Compute Infrastructure Program (up to $890M, open only to not-for-profits, post-secondaries and consortia) was unpacked by Torys. In Tech Policy Press, André Côté and Nancy Naylor argued the forthcoming national strategy must cover K-12, where few provinces or boards have responsible-use rules. In the UK, Computing at School's State of the Nation summary found 76% of teachers using AI but half of schools without an AI policy, and a two-to-one training gap between private and state schools. The Ada Lovelace Institute urged tougher evidence standards for AI productivity claims.
